{{Short description|Mathematical theorem}}
In [[Mathematical analysis|analysis]], the '''Fabry gap theorem''' is a result about the [[analytic continuation]] of [[Lacunary function|lacunary]] [[power series]]. Such a power series is "badly behaved" in the sense that it cannot be extended to be an [[analytic function]] anywhere on its [[radius of convergence|circle of convergence]]. It was proved by [[Eugène Fabry]] in 1896.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fabry |first=Eugène |date=1896 |title=Sur les points singuliers d'une fonction donnée par son développement en série et l'impossibilité du prolongement analytique dans des cas très généraux |url=http://www.numdam.org/item?id=ASENS_1896_3_13__367_0 |journal=Annales scientifiques de l'École normale supérieure |volume=13 |pages=367–399 |doi=10.24033/asens.431 |issn=0012-9593}}</ref>

==Statement of the theorem==

Let  <math>0<n_0<n_1<\dots</math> be a [[sequence]] of [[integer]]s such that the sequence <math>n_k/k</math> diverges to <math>\infty</math>, or equivalently<math display="block">D := \limsup_{k\to\infty} \frac{k}{n_k} = 0.</math>Let <math>(a_k)_{k\ge0}</math> be a sequence of [[complex number]]s such that the power series

:<math>f(z) = \sum_{k=0}^\infty a_k z^{n_k}</math>

has [[radius of convergence]] <math>1</math>. Then the unit circle is a [[natural boundary]] for the series ''<math>f</math>''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Erdős |first=P. |date=1945 |title=Note on the Converse of Fabry's Gap Theorem |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1990169?origin=crossref |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |volume=57 |issue=1 |pages=102 |doi=10.2307/1990169|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Boas |first=Ralph P. |title=Entire functions |date=1954 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-12-108150-8 |location=New York}}</ref>

The theorem may be deduced from the first main theorem of [[Turán's method]].

=== Converse statement ===
An exact [[Converse (logic)|converse]] to the theorem was established by [[George Pólya]] in 1942.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pólya |first=George |date=1942 |title=On converse gap theorems |url=https://www.ams.org/tran/1942-052-01/S0002-9947-1942-0006577-0/ |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=52 |issue=1 |pages=65–71 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1942-0006577-0 |issn=1088-6850}}</ref> If <math display="inline">D > 0</math>, then there exists a power series with exponent sequence <math>(n_k)_{k\ge0}</math> of radius of convergence equal to <math>1</math>, but for which the unit circle is not a natural boundary.

== Pólya's gap theorem ==
'''Pólya's gap theorem''',<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Koosis |first=Paul |title=The Logarithmic Integral II |date=1992 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-30907-3 |location=Cambridge, New York}}</ref> also known as the '''Fabry–Pólya theorem''',<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Martirosian |first=Valeri A. |date=2005-05-01 |title=The converse of the Fabry-Pólya theorem on singularities of lacunary power series |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/anly-2005-0203/html |journal=Analysis |language=en |volume=25 |issue=2 |pages=123–130 |doi=10.1515/anly-2005-0203 |issn=2196-6753|url-access=subscription }}</ref> is a refinement of the Fabry gap theorem. The theorem was proven by Fabry in 1899<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fabry |first=E. |date=1899 |title=Sur les séries de Taylor qui ont une infinité de points singuliers |url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.acta/1485882045 |journal=Acta Mathematica |language=en |volume=22 |issue= |pages=65–87 |doi=10.1007/BF02417871 |issn=0001-5962}}</ref> and put in its modern form by [[George Pólya|Pólya]] in 1929,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pólya |first=G. |date=1929 |title=Untersuchungen über Lücken und Singularitäten von Potenzreihen |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01180553 |journal=Mathematische Zeitschrift |language=de |volume=29 |issue=1 |pages=549–640 |doi=10.1007/BF01180553 |issn=0025-5874|url-access=subscription }}</ref> who also supplied a simpler proof. It states that every arc of the circle of convergence of length greater than <math>2\pi D</math> contains a [[Singularity (mathematics)|singularity]] of ''<math>f</math>''. When ''<math>D = 0</math>'', it follows that the singularities are [[Dense set|dense]] on the circle of convergence, which is the conclusion of the Fabry gap theorem. This extension also bears a converse.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
